text:
Before you read: look at the front cover


  1. What do you think will happen in the story?
    This is your prediction.
  2. What clues helped you make your prediction?
    Talk about what clues you can see, including the title and pictures.


During reading: stop and talk


  1. What might happen next?
    They might just guess, but encourage them to try using what they have already read to help.
  2. You could show them (model) how to use clues in the book to make a better prediction.
    Try asking questions as part of your model to get your child to add their own ideas, e.g. "That's interesting, I was thinking about how he found a key on the last page. I wonder what the key could be for? Do you think he might use it on the next page?"
  3. Carry on reading. Was your prediction correct?
    Remember, you don't need to be exactly right, as long as you had a thoughtful idea about what might happen. Sometimes authors like to surprise you!
  4. Stop and make more predictions later in the book.
    Can you use what you found out after your first prediction to help you this time?


After reading: challenge

What might happen if there was another book after this one?
Choose a book your child has not read before.You could do this with a book your child is reading, or one you are reading to them.
